questions: In hepatocellular injury such as acute viral hepatitis, ALT and AST dominate with values of*ten/10:How many multiples of ULN do transaminases typically reach in acute hepatitis?* above ten times the upper limit of normal.

In alcoholic liver disease the AST:ALT ratio, called the *De Ritis/de Ritis/DeRitis:This eponymous ratio uses AST divided by ALT to identify the cause of liver injury.* ratio, characteristically exceeds 2.
A raised ALP with a normal GGT suggests that the ALP comes from *bone:Which non-hepatic source of ALP does NOT raise GGT alongside it?* rather than from the biliary system.

In acute pancreatitis, serum amylase rises early but clears in three to five days, while *lipase:Which pancreatic enzyme stays elevated longer than amylase and has higher specificity?* remains elevated longer and is more specific for pancreatic disease.

The most specific marker of myocardial injury is *troponin/troponins/troponin I/troponin T:This gold-standard cardiac marker is not an enzyme but a structural protein of the sarcomere.*, a structural thin-filament protein that stays elevated for up to two weeks.

overallFeedback.feedback: Pattern recognition is the key to enzyme interpretation: transaminases >10× ULN with ALT leading points to hepatocellular injury; a De Ritis ratio (AST:ALT) >2 with induced GGT points to alcohol; ALP raised with normal GGT localises the source to bone; lipase is more specific and persistent than amylase for pancreatitis; and troponin, though not an enzyme, is the gold standard for myocardial injury owing to its tissue specificity and prolonged elevation.
